quotes.text: Your code never sees a secret. It doesn't store one. It doesn't read one from a config file. It just asks for a token and gets one.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the secretless authentication model in simple steps.

quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: If an attacker breaches your app, they can access what the identity has permission to access, but they can't steal the credential because there's nothing to steal.

quotes.text: In the new world, there are no secrets to check in. The credential doesn't exist in your code base or your config files.

quotes.text: Managed identities let you give your apps their own identity without ever touching a secret. That's the real shift from managing credentials to managing permissions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the mindset shift the episode argues for.

chapters.title: How it works under the hood
When not to use managed identities

takeaways: Managed identities give Azure resources their own Entra ID identity so code obtains tokens from IMDS instead of storing connection strings or client secrets.
Use system-assigned identities for a single resource with zero overhead and user-assigned identities when several resources share permissions or the identity must outlive them.
Managed identities only work for workloads running in Azure; outside Azure use service principals with Key Vault or workload identity federation.
hook: Connection strings in config files, leaked secrets on GitHub and certificates expiring at 3 a.m. are everyday pain for Azure teams. This episode explains managed identities in plain English for developers and cloud admins: the two types, how tokens are issued and where the limits are. You will learn how to replace secrets with permissions in your own workloads.
